> Author: researcher (vfx-deep-research workflow) · claude-sonnet-5-5 · default · 2026-10-12

# P4 case studies: destruction games (VFX and feel)

Scope: how breaking, debris, dust and collapse are made to feel heavy and satisfying. Extends, does not repeat, the physics/engine research already in the repo (`knowledge/research/the-finals-destruction-2026-10-06.md`, `teardown-optimization-2026-10-05.md`, `destruction-games-engines-2026-10-06.md`, `knowledge/reference/destruction-research-2026-10-02.md`). Those four were read first. They hold almost nothing on VFX, dust, sound or camera; the one reusable item is the owner-watched Teardown skyscraper clip (S34).

Method notes. (1) The web-search budget ran out mid-run (200/turn shared); the last ~12 sources were found by guessing known URLs or by following links from pages already read. (2) Fetched text was summarised by a small model before I saw it. Quotes below are as returned; verify against the page before any outside use. (3) PDFs and one Japanese page were converted locally (pdftotext, curl) and read in full text. (4) Honest headline: no maker published a destruction-VFX talk with timings in milliseconds. The numbers that exist are caps, camera/hit-stop anchors, a perception study and engine specs. Everything else is qualitative practice. Where a cell says "no number found" it means exactly that.

## 2. Findings

### 2a. Field methods

Fields: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition (Keyser/Riot framework). Timing words: windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation. [inf] marks my reasoning; the rest is sourced.

| field | method | what it does to the viewer | how to use it in a game | evidence level | source, tier and year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gameplay | One material tag drives VFX, decals, sound and fracture | Concrete reads as concrete, crate as crate, glass as glass; one object of several materials breaks per part and the layers agree | Give every brick a material tag. Look up particles, dust colour, chunk shape, sound and decal from that tag. Never hand-pick VFX per model | industry practice | Control (Remedy) GDC Summer 2020 via S12 (B). BF6 "same parameters ... for our audio systems" S01 (A, 2025) |
| gameplay | Material-driven emitters at seams and surfaces, fired by debris activation and by shockwave | Dust comes from where the thing actually broke, not a pasted puff | On brick-detach event spawn the emitter named by that brick's material at the break point; also spawn on shockwave pass | industry practice | S01 (A, 2025) |
| gameplay | Visual and audio language for "this can break" vs "this cannot"; audio tells you a hit landed | Player can plan and knows when damage worked | Fixed cue set per state: intact, damaged, about to fail, gone. Same audio cue on hit-landed even if no brick moved | industry practice | S02 (A, 2025, pre-alpha) |
| gameplay | Debris is a gameplay obstacle; make it bounce less and clutter less than reality | Fun beats fidelity; rubble stays traversable | Cap bounce count and settle quickly. Target debris you can walk over. Kyoto rework: "more traversable and less chaotic" | industry practice | S12 Control (B, 2020); S05 Finals (A, 2025) |
| gameplay | Hard caps on live physical debris; delay collisions and briefly disable bodies in big blasts; remove off-screen pieces | Keeps frame rate steady so the hit stays crisp | Budget N live bodies per view; stagger collision enable in blasts; despawn off-screen first. Control cap: 200 | industry practice | S12 (B, 2020). Compare repo cap in S34/R14 |
| gameplay | Pairing rule: if a destruction visual is missing, the audio is missing too (bug class) | Mismatch reads as broken | One data record per break type: {visual id, sound id}. Gate fails if one is empty | industry practice | S06 Finals (A, 2026) Kyoto fix |
| gameplay | Telegraph before a big failure: surface wear first, sag and lean, "a moment to react" | Anticipation (windup) turns a surprise into a read | Show cracks, dust trickle, creak and lean before a section drops. Gate the big drop behind a visible stress state | industry practice | S02 (A, 2025); S04 (A, 2026) |
| gameplay | Chain reactions and knock-on damage are the payoff; one event triggers the next | Escalation, crescendo | Let a falling piece break the next. VFX per link, scaled by piece mass | industry practice | S05 (A, 2025); S04 (A, 2026) |
| gameplay | Destruction is the product, not decoration; keep rock and ground unbreakable for readability | Player trusts what is solid | Keep a clear "solid" tier; do not dust-spam it | industry practice | S20 Teardown (A, 2020) |
| shape | Large chunks plus many small sprites | Big pieces carry weight; small ones carry scale and chaos | Three tiers: few physical chunks, many cosmetic bits, dust sprites. Map to bodies, client-only bits, particles | industry practice (S27 tier C needs a second source; S12 and S11 each use the same split: bodies plus particles) | S27 realtimevfx UnitFX (C, 2026); S12 (B, 2020); S11 (A, 2023) |
| shape | Texture particles with several silhouettes instead of extra polygon debris | Looks varied for cheap | For small bits use a flipbook with random start frame so each particle has its own shape | industry practice | S11 Bayonetta 3 (A, 2023). Roblox: FlipbookStartRandom + FlipbookFramerate 0 gives random static frames (S33 spec) |
| shape | Fracture that resembles real broken pieces; shape and material reflected in effects | Break looks like material, not cut-up cubes | Per-material chunk shape sets (splinters, slabs, shards). Seams hidden until damage | industry practice | S03 Finals (A, 2025); S08 (A, 2026) |
| shape | Collapse silhouette: apple-core, sag, lean, partial attachment | Readable state change over time; weight shows as lean before fall | Remove outer shell first and leave the core; sag then drop. Needs partial-attachment states | industry practice | S02 (A, 2025); S04 (A, 2026) |
| shape | Four dust kinds: debris, trail, impact, ambient. Debris dust is emitted from the chunks, with rotation | Dust follows pieces, so motion looks physical | Impact puff at hit, trail puffs behind falling chunks, drifting ambient haze after. Emitters parented to chunks | industry practice (film) | S15 DreamWorks Megamind (A, 2011, pre; no newer game confirmation except S27 dust on collision (C, 2026)) |
| shape | Dust sprite size from fall height; dust on sides when many small pieces fall | Taller drop = bigger cloud | Scale impact puff by drop distance. Also puff where a pile of small bits lands | industry practice | S27 (C, 2026), single source |
| shape | Brick-faithful effects: effect volumes replaced by bricks of matching size and shape; explosions subdivide bricks and jitter them | Toy identity survives the blast | In a brick game, effects are made of the same bricks or flat sprites in the brick palette; smaller bricks for finer detail | industry practice | S14 (A, 2014, pre); S18 (B, 2017). Newer: S17 (B, 2019) goes back to bricks. See conflicts |
| shape | Break along real connectivity: small groups detach, others stay together | Looks built, not random | Detach by connection groups (sub-assemblies), not single bricks | industry practice | S16 (B, 2014, pre); S14 (A, 2014, pre) |
| value | Light shards and dust with scene lights; point light tints particles (orange near orange light) | Debris sits in the scene, fire glows on it | Short-lived coloured light at blast; flipbook with LightInfluence on. Roblox exposes LightInfluence and LightEmission (S33 spec) | industry practice | S11 (A, 2023) |
| value | Do not let lingering smoke hide the fight: reduce lingering amount | Readability beats mood | Dust/smoke must clear on a set curve; tie lifetime to need to see | industry practice | S03 Finals, Thermal Bore change (A, 2025) |
| value | Smoke uses dithered transparency and a faked scattering via normals (reverse-engineered) | Soft look without true blending | Not needed in Roblox (alpha-blend). Lesson: dust opacity matters more than detail | industry practice (expert reverse-engineering) | S22 (C, 2023) |
| colour | Stay inside the licensed or house palette; fire = heat moves bricks through nearest allowed colours | Effects read as part of the toy world | Dust and debris take the colour of the source brick, shifted to the closest palette colour [inf for the tint rule] | industry practice | S18 (B, 2017) |
| colour | Hot energy effects sit on emissive/LightEmission with colour gradient over life | Flash then fade | Colour sequence over life: bright core to darker. Roblox Color/Transparency NumberSequence (S33 spec, tutorial) | spec | S33 |
| timing | Hit stop: freeze frames at impact; heavier hit = more frames | Weight and severity | Light 7 frames, heavy about 10 in Guilty Gear Xrd (games without hit stop rated dull). For brick hits scale frames with piece mass. Roblox has ParticleEmitter.TimeScale 0 to 1 to freeze or slow particles | study (preprint, comment analysis) + spec | S24 (preprint, 2022); S33 (spec) |
| timing | Sound must match the visual: delay or wrong sound ruins feel | Unnatural, cheap | Fire sound on the visible impact frame. Audio lead is noticed at smaller offsets than audio lag, so never early; a few frames late is safer [inf] | study + inference | S24 (preprint, 2022); S26 (study, 2015, n=19) |
| timing | Debris and dust animate one-shot across the particle's life | Clean puff then fade | Flipbook mode OneShot: frame rate = lifetime / frames (not the fps field). Max flipbook speed 30 fps | spec | S33 |
| timing | Scale sets speed: tiny toy-scale effects are fast and not slowed; large-scale VFX is normally slowed to sell size | Wrong speed breaks scale | Decide scale first. Small sparks and drips: short life, fast. Building-scale dust: long life, slow billow [inf for building side] | industry practice | S18 Ninjago (B, 2017); effect on 1s, characters on 2s S19 (B, 2017) |
| timing | Effects retimed to the host animation's frame rate | No mismatch between character and effect | Match effect update step to the rest of the scene | industry practice | S19 (B, 2017) |
| composition | Rigid bodies plus particles plus decals as three stacked layers; hide the original object when particles burst from joints | Cheap and still reads as shatter | Layer 1 bodies, layer 2 dust and sparks at joint breaks, layer 3 surface scars on what cannot break | industry practice | S12 Control (B, 2020) |
| composition | Persistent surface damage and decals on the unbreakable parts | Hits leave a record; scene shows history | Cracks and dents as decals on solid terrain after blasts | industry practice | S12 (B, 2020); S02 (A, 2025) |
| composition | Camera shake: trauma value 0 to 1; events add trauma; decays linearly; shake = trauma squared or cubed; noise not random | Big events feel big, small ones barely move the view; shake fits pause and slow motion | Each break adds trauma by mass; cubed curve; smooth noise. Eiserloh's own line: "Camera shake is like salt" | industry practice | S25 (A, 2016, pre); S24 (preprint, 2022) says camera effect/control is one of 3 deciding features |
| composition | Fade, never pop, for debris coming into and out of view | No visual glitch | Fade by distance; fade at despawn. Roblox Transparency NumberSequence | industry practice | S06 Finals (A, 2026) |
| composition | Check for orphans: floating leftovers after destruction are a repeating bug class | Floating props kill believability | Review checklist: after a collapse, scan for unsupported props (sandbags, branches, lamps, statues in the Finals notes) | industry practice | S03 (A, 2025); S06 (A, 2026) |
| composition | Do not simulate VFX or sound where no player is near | Saves budget | Gate emitters by distance to any viewer | industry practice | S05 Finals (A, 2025) |
| composition | Prioritise and cull destruction events and debris spawns per client | Many simultaneous blasts stay smooth | Server sends break events; each client decides how many cosmetic bits to spawn by distance and device | industry practice | S01 (A, 2025) |

### 2b. Breaking things

Timing per phase is the weak column. No maker source gives milliseconds per phase for any material. I list what exists and mark the rest "no number found". Phase words: windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

| moment | feeling | layers | timing per phase (ms or frames) | value and colour | shape and motion | camera and screen effect | sound sync point | what to leave out | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wood break (crate, plank, floor) | Snappy, splintery; hurts to be near | Bodies (planks), small splinter bits, a little dust, surface scar | no number found. Anchor: Roblox burst example for tiny bits life 0.2 to 0.6 s, speed 20 to 40 studs/s, drag 10 (S33 spec, a spark example, not wood) | Warm brown from the brick colour; keep dust light and short | Long thin splinters; remaining joists stay (R6 floors, S28); crate shatters per its own material (S12) | Small trauma only; no hit stop for small pieces [inf] | On the frame the first plank detaches | Smooth round chunks; long lingering haze [inf] | S12 (B, 2020); S28 (B, 2015, pre); S33 (spec) |
| stone / concrete (wall, slab) | Heavy, grainy, dusty | Bodies (slabs), fine rubble sprites, impact dust, trail dust, persistent decal cracks | no number found. ## 4. Conflicts between sources (newer first)

| topic | newer | older | what changed / how to settle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brick-made effects vs realistic simulated effects | LEGO Movie 2 (2019, S17): everything brick, little dust or smoke in the air | Ninjago (2017, S18/S19): real sims at minifig scale, only sometimes LEGO-like; LEGO Movie (2014, S14): all effects replaced by bricks | No trend; each film followed its art direction. Decide once for the game and record it. [inf] Our bricks are the world, so brick-palette or flat sprites in brick colours is the default; test realistic smoke only if the owner wants it. |
| Instant vs gradual collapse | Finals (S04, 2026; S05, 2025): sag, lean, partial attachment, collapse near the weak point | Finals earlier collapse model (not read; project doc says instant) and Teardown-style hard breaks | Direction of the field is gradual with a telegraph. No ms values published. |
| Lingering dust: weight vs readability | Finals (S03, 2025) cuts lingering smoke for visibility | Film practice (S15, 2011) has an "ambient" dust layer that lingers | Not a true conflict. Weight wants a lingering layer after the punch, readability wants it gone. Make lingering amount a per-game dial and test with the Roblox 20 s lifetime cap (S33). |
| Audio sync direction | S26 (2015): audio-lead detected sooner than audio-lag, but sensitivity (d') results inconsistent inside the same paper | none newer | Treat "sound never early, small late is OK" as a testable rule, not settled fact. |
| Debris realism | Control (S12) and Finals (S05) reduce bounce and chaos for play | Teardown (S20) leans on rich physical outcome and "precision work" | Same direction: keep the physics rich where it affects play, tame it where it is only visual. |
| Evidence on camera shake | S24 (2022): camera effect/control matters, no magnitudes | S25 (2016): concrete trauma curve | Newer source confirms the factor, not the numbers. Use S25 as the starting model. |
